questions.q: Why does this lesson argue that enrichment, not containment, is where most SOAR value shows up day to day?
options: Containment actions are technically impossible to automate in Sentinel
Enrichment is the only action type Logic Apps connectors support
An analyst's first minutes on a fresh incident are spent on retrieval -- who, how risky, what asset, where from -- which automation can do without needing judgment
Containment requires a paid Microsoft Defender license that most orgs don't have
questions.explain: Retrieving who the user is, their risk history, the asset involved, and the source location is pure lookup work with no judgment required -- exactly what's safe and valuable to automate.

questions.q: What does Microsoft Entra ID Protection's user risk score classify?
options: An account's low/medium/high risk level, built from sign-in anomalies and credential-leak signals
The CVSS severity of a vulnerability on the user's device
The business criticality tier of a host the user logged into
The geographic distance between two consecutive sign-ins only
questions.explain: The user risk score is Entra ID Protection's classification of an account, built from sign-in patterns, leaked credential matches, and anomaly detections.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say an incident touching a domain controller is not the same incident as one touching an ordinary workstation, even with identical other signals?
options: Domain controllers are immune to the alert types used in this course
Workstations cannot generate Sentinel incidents at all
Only domain controllers are tracked in SigninLogs
Asset criticality changes the stakes, and surfacing it automatically makes that difference visible immediately instead of twenty minutes into investigation
questions.explain: Asset criticality -- pulled from an inventory or watchlist -- flags that the two incidents carry very different stakes, and surfacing it automatically saves the analyst from discovering that fact late.

questions.q: What does the geo-IP enrichment step in this lesson actually produce?
options: An automatic decision to block the IP address
A country/city/ISP resolution for an entity IP, compared against the user's typical sign-in geography to flag whether it's consistent
A permanent firewall rule applied to the Sentinel workspace
A CVE lookup for the operating system behind that IP
questions.explain: Geo-IP enrichment resolves the IP entity's location and compares it to the user's normal sign-in pattern from SigninLogs -- a signal, not an action.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the key difference between pulling a user's risk score onto an incident and disabling that user's account based on the score?
options: There is no meaningful difference -- both are equally automatable without review
Disabling an account is always safer than displaying a risk score
Pulling the risk score assembles a fact for a human to see; disabling the account is a decision with real blast radius that this chapter does not let a playbook make unattended
Risk scores can only be viewed manually and cannot be queried with KQL
questions.explain: Enrichment assembles facts and surfaces them; containment changes real-world state. That distinction is exactly why containment gets a mandatory approval gate in the next lesson.
